editorial:
You follow Terry Richmond, a former Marine who just wants to bail his cousin out of jail. When small-town cops seize his cash under a shady civil forfeiture law, he refuses to back down. What starts as a simple money problem turns into a tense showdown with a corrupt police chief and his crew. The movie builds slowly but keeps you on edge the whole time, mixing quiet moments with sudden bursts of action that feel earned.

Aaron Pierre is fantastic as Terry, bringing calm strength and real emotion to every scene. Don Johnson is great as the corrupt chief you love to hate. The action feels grounded and real, not over-the-top. The pacing is steady, though the middle section drags a little before the big finale. If you enjoy smart thrillers with a strong lead and real stakes, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Terry storms the police station to confront Chief Burnne and his deputies. A tense shootout breaks out, and Terry takes down the corrupt officers one by one. He finally faces the chief, who tries to talk his way out before Terry kills him in self-defense. Terry then hands over the seized records to federal investigators, exposing the whole scheme. His cousin's name is cleared, and Terry walks away free, having brought justice to the town.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty crime thrillers with a strong lead.
